# Google

23 endpoints (22 GET, 1 POST). Base URL `https://www.socialcrawl.dev`, auth header `x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY`.

**Credit costs:** 11 standard (1 credit), 7 advanced (5), 5 custom (flat/metered) - the exact cost is in each endpoint heading below.

## GET /v1/google/ad - 5 credits (advanced)

Returns detailed information about a specific Google advertisement including ad copy, advertiser, and format. `post.published_at` is the ad's first appearance; the ad record itself does not carry it, so it is null unless you send `include=first_shown`. That reads one page of the advertiser's ads, at no extra credit, and fills the date when this creative is on it. Google publishes a first-shown date only for ads near the front of an advertiser's list, and that page's order changes, so an older or less prominent ad keeps a null date and `_warnings` says `first_shown_not_on_first_page`.

**Use when** Use it after company/ads to expand a single creative, since the list version does not carry the ad's own copy. No impression estimate is returned.
**Cost** cache 1800 s
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - Ads Transparency Center CREATIVE URL: must include both the advertiser and creative segments (`…/advertiser/{AR…}/creative/{CR…}`). Get one from `/v1/google/company/ads`. · e.g. `https://adstransparency.google.com/advertiser/AR01614014350098432001/creative/CR04647239345386815489`
- `include` (optional, enum: first_shown) - Send `first_shown` to fill `post.published_at` from the advertiser's ad list, at no extra credit. It fills only an ad on the first page of that list (Google dates only those); otherwise the date stays null and `_warnings` says `first_shown_not_on_first_page`.

**Response** `Post` object at `data`, `{ computed, post }` ([full schema](schemas/Post.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `post.content.text` | Post caption, description, or text content |
| `post.id` | Platform-specific post ID… |
| `post.url` | Direct URL to the post on the source platform |
| `post.author.username` | Author username |
| `computed.content_category` | Keyword-classified content category… |
| `computed.engagement_rate` | Computed engagement rate (0..1). |

+8 more (types in the full schema): `computed` {estimated_reach, language, save_rate}; `post.content` {media_urls, thumbnail_url}; `post.flags` {deleted}; `post.ext.ad` {format, last_shown_at}. Also in the sample: `post.author` {display_name string}; `post.ext` {hashtags null, mentions null}. Never filled: `post.author.avatar_url`, `post.author.verified`, `post.content.duration_seconds`, `post.engagement.comments`, `post.engagement.likes`, `post.engagement.saves`, `post.engagement.shares`, `post.flags.nsfw`, `post.flags.pinned`, `post.flags.spoiler`. Empty on every row the field-health check sampled (22/11/2026), so not returned today: `post.engagement.views`, `post.published_at`. Page-level: `data.hydration`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google/ad" \
  --data-urlencode "url=https://adstransparency.google.com/advertiser/AR01614014350098432001/creative/CR04647239345386815489" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/google/adlibrary/advertiser - 5 credits (advanced)

Returns the identity Google verified for an Ads Transparency advertiser: the legal name and country Google verified (`author.ext.verified_name`, `author.ext.verified_country_code`) beside the advertiser's display name, its country (`author.ext.country`) and its Transparency Center page.

**Use when** you want to confirm which company really stands behind an advertiser account. Pass the AR advertiser id from an advertiser search, or its Transparency Center URL.
**Cost** cache 900 s
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `id` (optional, string) - The advertiser id (AR followed by digits), as `/v1/google/adlibrary/advertisers/search` returns it. · e.g. `AR01614014350098432001`
- `url` (optional, string) - An Ads Transparency Center advertiser URL (`https://adstransparency.google.com/advertiser/AR...`).
- `region` (optional, string) - Two-letter country code to read the profile for.

**Constraints**

- Provide at least one of `id`, `url`.

**Response** `Author` object at `data`, `{ author, computed }` ([full schema](schemas/Author.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `author.id` | Platform-specific user ID… |
| `author.url` | Direct URL to the profile page |
| `author.display_name` | Display name or full name |
| `computed.content_category` | Keyword-classified content category… |
| `computed.engagement_rate` | Computed engagement rate (0..1). |
| `computed.estimated_reach` | Estimated reach based on views or follower count. |

+7 more (types in the full schema): `author.ext` {business_hours, country, products, verified_country_code, verified_name}; `computed` {language, save_rate}. Never filled: `author.avatar_url`, `author.bio`, `author.followers`, `author.following`, `author.joined_at`, `author.likes_count`, `author.posts_count`, `author.private`, `author.username`, `author.verified`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google/adlibrary/advertiser" \
  --data-urlencode "id=AR01614014350098432001" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/google/adlibrary/advertisers/search - 5 credits (advanced)

Searches the Google Ads Transparency Center for advertisers matching a query. Returns matching advertisers with `name`, `advertiser_id`, and `region`, plus their website domains. Defaults to US when `region` is omitted: pass a 2-letter country code (e.g. `AU`, `CA`) to search advertisers in another region.

**Use when** Use it first to look up the advertiser_id that company/ads needs when all you have is a brand name.
**Cost** cache 120 s
**Paging** single page - Fixed-window feed: upstream returns a single non-cursored result set.

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - Search keyword or phrase to find advertisers in the Google Ads Transparency Center. · e.g. `lululemon`
- `region` (optional, string) - 2-letter country code to search in. Defaults to US.

**Response** `AuthorList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ author }` ([full schema](schemas/AuthorList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `author.id` | Platform-specific user ID… |
| `author.display_name` | Display name or full name |
| `author.location` | ISO region code… |
| `author.ext.business_hours` | The page's opening hours as the source reports them. |
| `author.ext.products` | The products the company page lists, as the source sends… |

Never filled: `author.avatar_url`, `author.bio`, `author.followers`, `author.following`, `author.joined_at`, `author.likes_count`, `author.posts_count`, `author.url`, `author.username`, `author.verified`. Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google/adlibrary/advertisers/search" \
  --data-urlencode "query=lululemon" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/google/ai-overview - 1 credit (standard)

Returns the AI Overview Google shows at the top of its results for a query. `answer` is the text, `blocks` keep Google's layout (paragraphs, headings, lists with their items, tables as rows) with the sources each block rests on, and `sources` lists the cited pages numbered from 1 (index, url, title, site, snippet), the shape GET /v1/perplexity/research answers in. A query Google shows no AI Overview for returns 404 and is not charged. An answer takes about 10 to 15 seconds.

**Use when** you want to track what Google's AI says about a brand or topic, see which pages it cites, or monitor answers by country.
**Cost** cache 120 s
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - The search, up to 4,000 characters. · e.g. `how does a heat pump work`
- `country` (optional, string) - Two-letter country to ask from, for example us or gb.
- `language` (optional, string) - Language of the answer, for example en or de (default en).
- `location` (optional, string) - A city-level place to ask from, for example Austin, Texas.
- `device` (optional, enum: desktop | tablet | mobile) - desktop (default), tablet or mobile.

**Response** `Analytics` object at `data`, `{ answer, blocks, sources }` (from the response contract): {answer string, blocks array, sources array}; `blocks` {items array|null, language string|null, rows array|null, source_indexes array, text string|null, type string}; `blocks.items` {source_indexes array, text string|null, title string|null, url string|null}; `sources` {index integer, site string|null, snippet string|null, title string|null, url string}.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google/ai-overview" \
  --data-urlencode "query=how does a heat pump work" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/google/autocomplete - 1 credit (standard)

Returns the suggestions Google offers as someone types a partial query, about 10, in Google's order: each as `text` with its `position`, the row shape GET /v1/bing/suggestions answers in. type picks the list Google keeps for web (the default), YouTube, news, shopping or image searches; country and language localise it.

**Use when** you want it for keyword research, to see what people search around a topic or brand, or to compare suggestions across countries.
**Cost** cache 120 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Paging** single page - Google offers about 10 suggestions for a partial query, all in one call.

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - The partial query to complete, up to 100 characters. · e.g. `how to make`
- `country` (optional, string) - Two-letter country, for example us or gb (default us).
- `language` (optional, string) - Language of the suggestions, for example en or es (default en).
- `type` (optional, enum: web | youtube | news | shopping | images) - web (default), youtube, news, shopping or images.

**Response** `SearchResult` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ position, text }` (from the response contract): {position integer|null, text string|null}.

Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google/autocomplete" \
  --data-urlencode "query=how to make" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/google/business/contributor-reviews - 1-5 credits (request-shaped)

Returns the Google Maps reviews one reviewer has written, across every place they reviewed, newest first: each review's text, star rating, date, photos, the owner's reply, Google's aspect ratings (food, service, atmosphere) where given, and the place it is about in `review.ext.place` (name, address, coordinates, category, and its cid, also `review.entity_id`, to use on GET /v1/google/business/reviews). The page also carries the reviewer in `data.contributor`: name, avatar, Local Guide level, points, and how many reviews, ratings, photos, videos, answers and edits they have contributed. Identify the reviewer by `contributor_id` or by any Google Maps contributor link (`url`); every review's `author.url` on GET /v1/google/business/reviews is one. One call returns up to 200 reviews. A reviewer that does not exist returns 404 (auto-refunded). Use it to profile a reviewer, check whether a review comes from an established Local Guide, or find reviewers who post about many places on one day.

**Use when** a review looks suspicious or influential and you want to see everything that reviewer has posted, or to profile a Local Guide.
**Cost** price moves with `label` · cache 600 s
**Pricing** 1 credit per page. The default labels (sentiment, issue) are free. label=reports, incentivized or injection holds 4 extra credits and refunds down to 1 credit per started 25 reviews that were newly judged (the first 100 reviews of a page are judged): reviews already labelled are free, a page where nothing could be judged refunds the whole extra, and a cached page is free.
**Paging** single page - One call returns up to `limit` reviews (max 200); the source has no page cursor.

**Query params**

- `contributor_id` (optional, string) - The reviewer's Google Maps contributor id: the 10 to 32 digits in their profile link (for example 102611939832726470161). · e.g. `102611939832726470161`
- `url` (optional, string) - A Google Maps contributor link, for example https://www.google.com/maps/contrib/102611939832726470161/reviews. The `author.url` of any review on GET /v1/google/business/reviews works.
- `limit` (optional, integer, 1-200) - How many reviews to return, from 1 to 200 (default 100), newest first. The price is the same at any limit. · e.g. `50`
- `language` (optional, string) - Language for review labels and place names, for example en or fr (default en).
- `country` (optional, string) - Two-letter country for localisation, for example us or fr.
- `since` (optional, string) - Rows published from this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or ISO 8601. Rows older than it are left off each page. This list is not in date order, so the walk does not stop at the date: keep following `next_cursor`, and each page costs what a page costs even when every row on it is filtered out. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until).
- **Shared controls** `label` (sentiment | issue | reports | incentivized | injection; paid: reports, incentivized, injection) · `label_evidence` (1) · `reports` → [labels](api-overview.md#labels-relevance-and-quality); `until` → [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until)

**Constraints**

- Provide at least one of `contributor_id`, `url`.
- `reports`, `label_evidence` are no-ops without `label` - sending one alone is a free 400.
- `goal`, `fit_tokens` are no-ops without `fit` - sending one alone is a free 400.
- `label`: at most 5 comma-separated values.

**Response** `ReviewList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ computed, review }` ([full schema](schemas/ReviewList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `review.text` | Full review body |
| `review.id` | Review ID (parsed from the review URL when not first-class) |
| `review.published_at` | Review creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string… |
| `review.url` | URL of the review. |
| `review.author.name` | Reviewer name. |
| `review.author.url` | URL of the reviewer's profile. |

+14 more (types in the full schema): `computed` {labels_evidence}; `review` {entity_id, language}; `computed.labels` {incentivized, injection, issue, reports, sentiment}; `review.author` {avatar_url, reviews_count}; `review.ext` {google, place}; `review.rating` {max, value}. Also in the sample: `review` {translated boolean, images string[]}; `review.responses[]` {id null, author string, text string} (+1 more). Never filled: `review.author.location`, `review.source`, `review.title`, `review.verified`. Empty on every row the field-health check sampled (22/11/2026), so not returned today: `review.helpful_votes`, `review.original_language`. Page-level: `data.contributor`, `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.estimate`, `data.held_back`, `data.labels`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google/business/contributor-reviews" \
  --data-urlencode "contributor_id=102611939832726470161" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/google/business/extended-reviews - 5-9 credits (request-shaped)

Returns reviews of a place aggregated from the Google reviews element, not only Google users but reputable third-party sources (TripAdvisor, Yelp, Trustpilot). Each review carries its source domain, full text (with original-language translation), star rating, reviewer stats, and owner replies. Identify the place by keyword, cid, or place_id.

**Use when** you want a place's reviews from Google and third party sites together, rather than product or app reviews.
**Cost** price moves with `label` · cache 600 s
**Pricing** 5 credits per page. The default labels (sentiment, issue) are free. label=reports, incentivized or injection holds 4 extra credits and refunds down to 1 credit per started 25 reviews that were newly judged (the first 100 reviews of a page are judged): reviews already labelled are free, a page where nothing could be judged refunds the whole extra, and a cached page is free.
**Paging** single page - Depth-based fan-out: page size is controlled by depth, one call.

**Query params**

- `keyword` (optional, string) - Business name + address. Use cid/place_id for an exact match. · e.g. `Irving Farm New York 645 5th Ave`
- `cid` (optional, string) - Google customer id (cid) of the place.
- `place_id` (optional, string) - Google place_id of the place.
- `location_name` (optional, string) - Geographic context as 'City,Region,Country'.
- `language_name` (optional, string) - Result language (default 'English').
- `depth` (optional, integer) - Number of reviews to return (default 20, step 20, max 1000).
- `since` (optional, string) - Rows published from this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or ISO 8601. Rows older than it are left off each page. This list is not in date order, so the walk does not stop at the date: keep following `next_cursor`, and each page costs what a page costs even when every row on it is filtered out. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until).
- **Shared controls** `label` (sentiment | issue | reports | incentivized | injection; paid: reports, incentivized, injection) · `label_evidence` (1) · `reports` → [labels](api-overview.md#labels-relevance-and-quality); `until` → [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until)

**Constraints**

- Provide at least one of `keyword`, `cid`, `place_id`.
- `reports`, `label_evidence` are no-ops without `label` - sending one alone is a free 400.
- `goal`, `fit_tokens` are no-ops without `fit` - sending one alone is a free 400.
- `label`: at most 5 comma-separated values.

**Response** `ReviewList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ computed, review }` ([full schema](schemas/ReviewList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `review.text` | Full review body |
| `review.id` | Review ID (parsed from the review URL when not first-class) |
| `review.published_at` | Review creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string… |
| `review.url` | URL of the review. |
| `review.author.name` | Reviewer name. |
| `review.author.url` | URL of the reviewer's profile. |

+15 more (types in the full schema): `computed` {labels_evidence}; `review` {entity_id, images, responses, source, translated}; `computed.labels` {incentivized, injection, issue, reports, sentiment}; `review.author` {avatar_url, reviews_count}; `review.rating` {max, value}. Never filled: `review.author.location`, `review.helpful_votes`, `review.language`, `review.title`, `review.verified`. Empty on every row the field-health check sampled (22/11/2026), so not returned today: `review.original_language`. Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.estimate`, `data.held_back`, `data.labels`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google/business/extended-reviews" \
  --data-urlencode "keyword=Irving Farm New York 645 5th Ave" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/google/business/info - 1 credit (standard)

Returns the full Google Business Profile (Maps / Knowledge Panel) for a local business: name, category, rating, address, phone, coordinates, hours, attributes, and claimed status. Identify the place by keyword, cid, or place_id (cid/place_id are most reliable). A lookup by keyword alone can come back without `ext.attributes`, `ext.people_also_search` and `ext.status`; pass cid or place_id for the complete profile.

**Use when** you want to look up one local business by keyword, cid, or place_id before pulling its reviews, questions, or updates.
**Cost** cache 900 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `keyword` (optional, string) - Business name + address (e.g. 'Irving Farm New York 645 5th Ave'). Use cid/place_id when known for an exact match. · e.g. `Irving Farm New York 645 5th Ave`
- `cid` (optional, string) - Google customer id (cid) of the place: the most reliable identifier.
- `place_id` (optional, string) - Google place_id of the place.
- `location_name` (optional, string) - Geographic context as 'City,Region,Country'. Without it, a keyword that looks Polish (a Polish postcode or Polish-only letters) is searched in Poland and every other keyword in 'New York,New York,United States'.
- `language_name` (optional, string) - Result language (default 'English').

**Constraints**

## GET /v1/google/business/reviews - 5-54 credits (request-shaped)

Returns the Google reviews of one place on Google Maps, newest first by default: full text (translated into `language` when written in another, with the original kept in `ext.google.original_text`), star rating, likes, photos, the owner's reply, the reviewer's name, profile and review count, and whether they are a Local Guide. Restaurant and hotel reviews also carry Google's aspect ratings (food, service, atmosphere) in `ext.google.aspects`. Identify the place by place_id or cid: GET /v1/google/business/search returns both for every place it finds (`place.ext.place_id`, and `place.id`, which is the cid). One call returns up to 1,000 reviews. Use `since` to pull only reviews published after a date, and `query` to keep only reviews that mention a word or phrase. Send `topics=true` to also get the place's review topics in `data.topics` (each with its id, keyword and how many reviews mention it), and `topic` with one of those ids to get only the reviews about that topic (up to 30). Only Google-sourced reviews are returned; GET /v1/google/business/extended-reviews also aggregates third-party sites.

**Use when** you have found a local business with business search and want what its customers say on Google, filtered by date or by a word.
**Cost** price moves with `depth`, `label` · cache 600 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Pricing** 5 credits per started 100 reviews returned (5 for up to 100, 50 for 1,000). The hold is set by `depth` and refunded down to the reviews that came back, so a place with 37 reviews costs 5 at any depth. The default labels (sentiment, issue) are free. label=reports, incentivized or injection holds 4 extra credits and refunds down to 1 credit per started 25 reviews that were newly judged (the first 100 reviews of a page are judged): reviews already labelled are free, a page where nothing could be judged refunds the whole extra, and a cached page is free.
**Paging** single page - Depth-based: one call returns up to depth reviews (max 1,000). The source has no page cursor.

**Query params**

- `place_id` (optional, string) - Google place_id of the place (for example ChIJqdNaaBVbwokRLTafYrQlZI8). GET /v1/google/business/search returns it as `place.ext.place_id`. · e.g. `ChIJqdNaaBVbwokRLTafYrQlZI8`
- `cid` (optional, string) - Google customer id (cid) of the place, a decimal number. GET /v1/google/business/search returns it as `place.id`.
- `depth` (optional, integer, 1-1000) - How many reviews to return, from 1 to 1,000 (default 100). Billed per started 100 reviews that come back.
- `sort` (optional, enum: newest | relevant | highest | lowest) - Review order: newest (default), relevant, highest or lowest rating.
- `since` (optional, string) - Only reviews published on or after this date, as YYYY-MM-DD or an ISO-8601 timestamp. Pair it with sort=newest to pull just the reviews added since your last call.
- `query` (optional, string) - Only reviews whose text contains this word or phrase (for example 'crust' or 'parking').
- `language` (optional, string) - Two-letter language code reviews are translated into (default 'en'). A review written in this language is returned as written.
- `topic` (optional, string) - Only the reviews about one topic: an id from data.topics (topics=true). Up to 30 reviews (depth defaults to 30 and is at most 30), in Google's order for the topic, so sort and since do not combine with it.
- `topics` (optional, boolean) - When true, the page also carries the place's review topics in data.topics, as Google lists them: each with its id (send it back as `topic`), its keyword (for example 'long lines') and how many reviews mention it. depth is at most 100 with topics=true, and since does not combine with it. Default false.
- **Shared controls** `label` (sentiment | issue | reports | incentivized | injection; paid: reports, incentivized, injection) · `label_evidence` (1) · `reports` → [labels](api-overview.md#labels-relevance-and-quality)

**Constraints**

- Provide at least one of `place_id`, `cid`.
- `reports`, `label_evidence` are no-ops without `label` - sending one alone is a free 400.
- `goal`, `fit_tokens` are no-ops without `fit` - sending one alone is a free 400.
- `label`: at most 5 comma-separated values.

**Response** `ReviewList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ computed, review }` ([full schema](schemas/ReviewList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `review.text` | Full review body |
| `review.id` | Review ID (parsed from the review URL when not first-class) |
| `review.published_at` | Review creation timestamp as an ISO 8601 UTC string… |
| `review.url` | URL of the review. |
| `review.author.name` | Reviewer name. |
| `review.author.url` | URL of the reviewer's profile. |

+18 more (types in the full schema): `computed` {labels_evidence}; `review` {entity_id, helpful_votes, images, language, original_language, responses, translated}; `computed.labels` {incentivized, injection, issue, reports, sentiment}; `review.author` {avatar_url, reviews_count}; `review.ext` {google}; `review.rating` {max, value}. Never filled: `review.author.location`, `review.source`, `review.title`, `review.verified`. Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.estimate`, `data.held_back`, `data.labels`, `data.topics`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google/business/reviews" \
  --data-urlencode "place_id=ChIJqdNaaBVbwokRLTafYrQlZI8" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## POST /v1/google/business/reviews/history - 5-500 credits (request-shaped)

Starts a background job (202) that collects up to `depth` Google reviews (1 to 10,000) of one place, newest first. Use it when a place has more reviews than the 1,000 one GET /v1/google/business/reviews call returns. The body takes exactly one of `place_id` or `cid` (both from GET /v1/google/business/search) and `depth`; any other field is a free 400. The 202 returns `data.job_id`, `status`, `credits_hold`, `credits_charged` (null until the job settles) and `expires_at` (7 days). A run that cannot start is a refunded 502. Read the reviews 100 at a time with GET /v1/google/business/reviews/history/{job_id}?offset=&limit=, which costs 0 credits and returns the same review objects as GET /v1/google/business/reviews. Until the job settles that read returns the job alone; after it, each page also carries `data.job` with the final `status` and `credits_charged`.

**Use when** a place has more reviews than the 1,000 one business reviews call returns and you need every one of them.
**Cost** price depends on how many items the request sends or returns · not cached
**Pricing** 5 credits per started 100 reviews collected, the same rate as GET /v1/google/business/reviews. Submitting holds the price of `depth` and refunds down to the reviews collected when the job settles; a job that collects none is refunded in full.
**Execution** Async job. The start response is a job id. Read pages with GET /v1/google/business/reviews/history/{job_id}?offset=&limit=. That read costs 0 credits.
**Paging** none

**Body params** (JSON)

- `depth` (required) - How many reviews to collect, an integer from 1 to 10,000. Page the result with GET /v1/google/business/reviews/history/{job_id}?offset=&limit=. · e.g. `7366`
- `place_id` (optional, string) - Google place_id of the place. GET /v1/google/business/search returns it as `place.ext.place_id`. · e.g. `ChIJqdNaaBVbwokRLTafYrQlZI8`
- `cid` (optional, string) - Google customer id (cid) of the place, a decimal number. GET /v1/google/business/search returns it as `place.id`.

**Constraints**

- Provide at least one of `place_id`, `cid`.

**Response** `Analytics` async job: this call returns `job_id`; poll `GET /v1/google/business/reviews/history/{job_id}` for status, and the result comes back there once it completes. Job envelope (inferred from a sample): {job_id string, status string, credits_hold number, credits_charged null, expires_at string}.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google/business/reviews/history" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"depth":7366,"place_id":"ChIJqdNaaBVbwokRLTafYrQlZI8"}'
```

## GET /v1/google/business/search - 5 credits (advanced)

Returns the Google Maps businesses for a keyword or category in a place, in Google's own order: name, cid, place_id, address, phone, website, category and additional categories, star rating and review count, coordinates, claimed status and opening hours. `place.id` is the cid, so any row chains into GET /v1/google/business/info?cid= or /v1/google/business/extended-reviews?cid=. `place.ext` adds `place_id`, `maps_url`, `domain`, `rank`, `city`, `postal_code`, `region`, `country_code`, `hours`, `status` (open, close, temporarily_closed or closed_forever), `business_status` (operational, closed_temporarily or closed_permanently), `closed` (true when closed for good), `temporarily_closed`, `data_id` and `booking_url`. Narrow the places with the filters Google Maps itself offers: `min_rating`, and one opening filter (`open_now`, `open_24h`, or `open_on_day` with an optional `open_at_hour`). A filtered search also fills `status_description` (the line Google shows, such as "Open · Closes 4 AM"), `order_url` and `knowledge_graph_id`, and leaves `place.verified`, `city`, `postal_code` and `region` null (said on `data._warnings`). Give the place as `location` ("Milano, Italy", a country, or a full "City,Region,Country" name such as "Milan,Lombardy,Italy") or as `lat` + `lng` (with an optional `zoom`); sending neither, or both, is a free 400. Sponsored listings are left out. A flat 5 credits for up to 100 places; a search with no results returns an empty list and is not billed.

**Use when** you want to build a list of local businesses by trade and area, such as dentists in Milano, then pass a cid to business/info for the full profile.
**Cost** cache 120 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Paging** single page - Depth-based: `limit` (1-100) sets how many places one call returns; Google Maps serves no further page.

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - What to look for, as you would type it into Google Maps: a category or trade ('dentista', 'ristorante', 'commercialista') or a business name. Use the local language for local results. · e.g. `dentista`
- `location` (optional, string) - Where to search: 'City, Country' (e.g. 'Milano, Italy'), a country name or ISO code ('Italy', 'IT'), or a full City,Region,Country name ('Milan,Lombardy,Italy'). Required unless lat and lng are sent. · e.g. `Milano, Italy`
- `lat` (optional, string) - Latitude of the search centre (-90 to 90). Send with lng instead of location.
- `lng` (optional, string) - Longitude of the search centre (-180 to 180). Send with lat instead of location.
- `zoom` (optional, integer, 3-21) - Google Maps zoom level around lat/lng, 3 (continent) to 21 (street). Defaults to 14, about a city district. Only with lat/lng.
- `language` (optional, string) - Language code for the results ('it', 'en', 'de'). Defaults to the main language of the country in location ('it' for Italy), or 'en' for coordinates.
- `limit` (optional, integer, 1-100) - How many places to return, 1-100 (default 20). The price is the same at any limit.
- `min_rating` (optional, string) - Only places rated at least this, one of Google Maps' steps: 2, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 4 or 4.5.
- `open_now` (optional, boolean) - true to keep only places open now (in the place's own time). Not with open_24h or open_on_day.
- `open_24h` (optional, boolean) - true to keep only places open 24 hours. Not with open_now or open_on_day.
- `open_on_day` (optional, enum: mon | tue | wed | thu | fri | sat | sun) - Only places open on this day: mon, tue, wed, thu, fri, sat or sun. Add open_at_hour for a time of that day.
- `open_at_hour` (optional, integer, 0-23) - With open_on_day: only places open at this hour of that day, 0 to 23 (23 is 11 PM).

**Constraints**

- Provide at least one of `location`, `lat`.
- `lat` is a no-op without `lng` - sending it alone is a free 400.
- `lng` is a no-op without `lat` - sending it alone is a free 400.
- `zoom` is a no-op without `lat` - sending it alone is a free 400.

**Response** `PlaceList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ place }` ([full schema](schemas/PlaceList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `place.id` | Place ID… |
| `place.name` | Business / hotel name |
| `place.url` | Website or canonical URL |
| `place.address` | Street address as the source prints it. |
| `place.categories` | Additional categories beyond the primary one. |
| `place.category` | Primary category… |

+8 more (types in the full schema): `place` {image_urls, latitude, longitude, phone, reviews_count, verified}; `place.rating` {max, value}. Also in the sample: `place.ext` {status string, place_id string}; `place.ext.hours[]` {date null, day_name string, is_open boolean, opens_at string, closes_at string}; `place.ext.rating_distribution` {1 number, 2 number, 3 number, 4 number} (+8 more). Never filled: `place.description`. Empty on every row the field-health check sampled (22/11/2026), so not returned today: `place.price_level`. Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google/business/search" \
  --data-urlencode "query=dentista" \
  --data-urlencode "location=Milano, Italy" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/google/company/ads - 5 credits (advanced)

Returns ads from a specific company/domain in the Google Ads Transparency Center. Each ad includes creative, format, and date range.

**Use when** you want to page through an advertiser's whole ad history by domain or advertiser_id, filtered by date, placement, or format.
**Cost** cache 1800 s
**Paging** cursor · ≈40/page (observed once) · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/40) x 5 credits · typical 1.0-2.3 s

**Query params**

- `domain` (optional, string) - Company domain name to look up ads for · e.g. `lululemon.com`
- `advertiser_id` (optional, string) - The advertiser id of the company
- `topic` (optional, enum: all | political) - The topic to search for. If you search for 'political', you will also need to pass a 'region', like 'US' or 'AU'
- `region` (optional, string) - The region to search for. Defaults to anywhere
- `start_date` (optional, string) - Start date to search for. Format: YYYY-MM-DD
- `end_date` (optional, string) - End date to search for. Format: YYYY-MM-DD
- `platform` (optional, enum: google_maps | google_play | google_search | google_shopping | youtube) - Google surface to filter ads by (e.g. youtube, google_search)
- `format` (optional, enum: text | image | video) - Ad format to filter by: text, image, or video
- `get_ad_details` (optional, string) - Set to true to get the ad details. Will cost 25 credits.
- `cursor` (optional, string) - Cursor to paginate through results
- `since` (optional, string) - Rows published from this date: YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or ISO 8601. Rows older than it are left off each page. This list is not in date order, so the walk does not stop at the date: keep following `next_cursor`, and each page costs what a page costs even when every row on it is filtered out. Aliases: [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until).
- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages); `until` → [date window](api-overview.md#date-window-since-until)

## GET /v1/google/hotels/search - 1 credit (standard)

Returns hotels for a query from Google Travel: name, star rating, review score, coordinates, images, and nightly price. Dates default to next-day / one-night / two-visitors when omitted. Without `location_name`, the place the keyword names sets where Google searches: `hotels in Paris` is searched in France and `hotels in Paris, TX` in the United States; a keyword that names no place (`cheap hotels`) is searched from New York. Send `location_name` to set it yourself. Each hotel_identifier can be passed to GET /v1/google/hotels/info for full detail. When the first source is unavailable a second source answers: its `place.id` is Google's map id for the hotel, which hotels/info does not take, `place.hotel.stars` is null, and `data._warnings` says so.

**Use when** you want to find candidate hotels for a place or keyword, then pass a hotel_identifier to hotels/info for the full record.
**Cost** cache 120 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Paging** single page - Depth-based fan-out: page size is controlled by depth, one call.

**Query params**

- `keyword` (required) - Hotel search query (e.g. 'hotels in New York'). · e.g. `hotels in New York`
- `location_name` (optional, string) - Geographic context as 'City,Region,Country'. When omitted, the country of the place the keyword names (New York when it names none).
- `language_name` (optional, string) - Result language (default 'English').
- `check_in` (optional, string) - Check-in date (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to the next day.
- `check_out` (optional, string) - Check-out date (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to one night.

**Response** `PlaceList` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ place }` ([full schema](schemas/PlaceList.md))

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `place.id` | Place ID… |
| `place.name` | Business / hotel name |
| `place.category` | Primary category… |
| `place.image_urls` | Image URL, or a list of image URLs, for the place. |
| `place.latitude` | Latitude in decimal degrees. |
| `place.longitude` | Longitude in decimal degrees. |

+10 more (types in the full schema): `place` {reviews_count}; `place.hotel` {amenities, check_in_time, check_out_time, prices, review_topics, stars, stars_description}; `place.rating` {max, value}. Never filled: `place.address`, `place.description`, `place.phone`, `place.price_level`, `place.url`, `place.verified`. Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`.

**Next** `google/hotels/info` (`hotel_identifier` ← `data.items[].place.id`) - Get Google hotel detail.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google/hotels/search" \
  --data-urlencode "keyword=hotels in New York" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/google/images - 1 credit (standard)

Returns Google Images results for a query, up to 100 a page: the full-size image with its width and height, Google's thumbnail, the title, the page the image sits on and the site, and, when Google lists them, the licence link, creator, credit and copyright. license narrows the results to images Google lists under those usage rights (creative_commons, commercial_and_other, free_to_share, free_to_share_commercially, free_to_modify, free_to_modify_commercially). safe_search=strict filters explicit images, off turns the filter off, and moderate (the default) is Google's own setting. An image Google embeds without a link has image_url null and keeps its thumbnail. Pass the returned cursor for the next page; Google repeats some images across pages, so a page leaves out any image an earlier page of the same walk served, and data._warnings says how many. A search usually reaches about 200 images in two pages.

**Use when** you want to find images for a topic or product, collect openly licensed images, or see which sites rank in image search.
**Cost** cache 120 s
**Paging** cursor · ≈100/page (observed once); set with `limit` · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/100) x 1 credits

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - What to search for, up to 2,048 characters. · e.g. `red bicycle`
- `country` (optional, string) - Two-letter country to search from, for example us or gb.
- `language` (optional, string) - Language of Google's interface, for example en or de (default en).
- `safe_search` (optional, enum: strict | moderate | off) - strict, moderate (default, Google's own setting) or off.
- `license` (optional, enum: creative_commons | commercial_and_other | free_to_share | free_to_share_commercially | free_to_modify | free_to_modify_commercially) - Only images Google lists under these usage rights.
- `device` (optional, enum: desktop | tablet | mobile) - desktop (default), tablet or mobile.
- `limit` (optional, integer, 1-100) - Images a page, 1 to 100 (default 100).
- `cursor` (optional, string) - The next_cursor from a previous page of the same search. Omit for the first page.
- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages)

**Response** `MediaList` rows at `data.items[]` (inferred from a sample): {id string, position number, title string, image_url string, thumbnail_url string, width number, height number, thumbnail_width number, thumbnail_height number, page_url string, source string, license_url null, creator null, credit null, copyright null}.

Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.walk`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google/images" \
  --data-urlencode "query=red bicycle" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/google/keyword-volume - 16 credits (custom)

Returns Google monthly search volume, cost per click, competition, and a 12-month trend for up to 20 keywords in one country. Response is `{ location, location_name, language, items }`: each item carries `keyword`, `search_volume` (average monthly searches), `cpc` with its `currency`, `competition` (0 to 1) with `competition_level`, `monthly_searches` (the last 12 months, oldest first, as `{ year, month, search_volume }`) and, where Google classifies it, `search_intent`. Use it to compare demand for a product across markets: call it once per country with the same keywords. You get one item per keyword you asked for, in your order. A keyword Google holds no volume for comes back with `search_volume: null`, never 0, so a null means unknown and a 0 means Google reports none. Every null row says why in `null_reason`: `"withheld"` means Google stopped publishing volume for the term (since December 2023 it withholds many health and other sensitive terms, such as "shingles" or "herniated disc"), and such a row carries `last_reported` (`{ year, month, search_volume }`, the last month Google published a figure) with an empty `monthly_searches`; `"no_data"` means Google holds no figure at all (very rare or unknown terms). For relative interest in a withheld term, use `/v1/google_trends/explore`, or `/v1/naver/search-trend` in Korea. When no keyword has current volume the call returns 404 and costs 0 credits; its message lists the last published figures. Volumes are Google's own rounded monthly averages and are refreshed monthly, so results are cached for 24 hours. Typical latency is 2 seconds. Priced at a flat 16 credits per call whatever the keyword count, so send all 20 at once.

**Use when** you want to compare demand for a product across countries by calling it once per country with the same keywords.
**Cost** cache 86400 s
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `keywords` (required) - 1-20 comma-separated keywords (e.g. 'lip gloss,lip oil'). Each keyword may be up to 80 characters. Duplicates are ignored. More than 20 keywords, or a keyword over 80 characters, is rejected with a free 400 before the request is billed. · e.g. `lip gloss,lip oil`
- `location` (optional, string) - Country as an ISO code ('US', 'GB', 'KR'), a full country name ('United Kingdom', 'South Korea') or a numeric location code ('2826'). Defaults to the United States. Volume is published for 94 countries; any other location is rejected with a free 400 naming the accepted forms. · e.g. `GB`
- `language` (optional, string) - Language code ('en', 'de', 'ko') the keywords are searched in. Defaults to the first language listed for the country: Germany is 'de' and Belgium is 'fr', but Vietnam, Indonesia, India, Malaysia, Pakistan, the Philippines, Hong Kong and Singapore default to 'en', so pass their local language (e.g. 'vi', 'id', 'hi') explicitly. A language the country does not hold (Germany in English) is rejected with a free 400 listing the ones it does.

**Constraints**

- `keywords`: at most 20 comma-separated values.

**Response** `Analytics` rows at `data.items[]` (inferred from a sample): {keyword string, search_volume number, cpc number, currency string, competition number, competition_level string, search_intent string, monthly_searches array, null_reason string}; `monthly_searches[]` {year number, month number, search_volume number}; `last_reported` {year number, month number, search_volume number}.

Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.items`, `data.language`, `data.location`, `data.location_name`, `data.next_cursor`, `data.total`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google/keyword-volume" \
  --data-urlencode "keywords=lip gloss,lip oil" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/google/patents - 1 credit (standard)

Returns Google Patents publications for a query, 10, 25, 50 or 100 a page (default 10), with Google's total: the publication number with its patent office and kind code (B2 is a granted US patent, A1 an application), title, Google Patents link, the passage Google matched, the first inventor, the assignee, the priority, filing, publication and grant dates (grant_date is null for an application not granted), and the PDF when there is one. country limits the search to one patent office (US, EP, WO and others); status picks all publications, granted patents or applications; sort=newest or oldest orders by filing date. The query takes keywords, quoted phrases and publication numbers. Pass the returned cursor for the next page; Google serves up to 100 pages.

**Use when** you want to search prior art, track a company's or a technology's patent filings, or list the newest grants in a field.
**Cost** cache 120 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Paging** cursor · ≈10/page (observed once); set with `limit` · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/10) x 1 credits

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - Keywords, a quoted phrase or a publication number, up to 500 characters. · e.g. `solid state battery`
- `country` (optional, string) - A two-letter patent office code, for example US, EP or WO.
- `status` (optional, enum: all | grant | application) - all (default), grant or application.
- `sort` (optional, enum: relevance | newest | oldest) - relevance (default), newest or oldest (by filing date).
- `limit` (optional, enum: 10 | 25 | 50 | 100) - Publications a page: 10 (default), 25, 50 or 100.
- `cursor` (optional, string) - The next_cursor from a previous page of the same search. Omit for the first page.
- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages)

**Response** `SearchResult` rows at `data.items[]` (from the response contract): {assignee string|null, filing_date string|null, grant_date string|null, id string|null, inventor string|null, kind string|null, office string|null, pdf_url string|null, position integer|null, priority_date string|null, publication_date string|null, snippet string|null, title string|null, url string|null}.

Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.walk`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google/patents" \
  --data-urlencode "query=solid state battery" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/google/search - 1 credit (standard)

Returns Google search results for a query. Each result includes title, URL, and a text snippet. Google's own operators work in the query: `site:theqoo.net 다한증` returns only pages from that site (measured 09/10/2026: every row on the named domain), which makes this the cheapest way to find posts on one forum or community before reading them with /v1/web/scrape. Ten results a page; `page` walks further. A query with no results (common for a `site:` search) is a free `200` with `items: []` and `empty_reason: "no_matches"`, never a 404.

**Use when** you want it for general web results; for Korean web pages use naver/webkr/search, and for news headlines use google_news/search.
**Cost** cache 120 s · multi-source (billed once)
**Empty results** An upstream 404 means "zero items", not "not found" - you get `200 {items: []}` and a refund.
**Paging** page (native `page`) · ≈10/page (observed once) · depth unknown · N items ≈ ceil(N/10) x 1 credits · typical 2.2-8.2 s

**Query params**

- `query` (required) - Search keyword or phrase. Google operators such as site:example.com work. · e.g. `best restaurants in London`
- `region` (optional, string) - 2 letter country code, ie US, UK, CA, KR, etc This will show results from that country
- `date_posted` (optional, enum: last-hour | last-day | last-week | last-month | last-year) - Only pages Google dates within this window: last-hour, last-day, last-week, last-month or last-year. The strongest recency filter for forum and community posts.
- `page` (optional, integer) - Page number to retrieve
- **Shared controls** `max_pages` (1-50) → [walks](api-overview.md#search-filters-and-multi-page-walks); `max_items` (1-5000) · `max_credits` (1-100000) → [one-call walks](api-overview.md#get-more-in-one-call-max_items-max_credits-max_pages)

**Response** `SearchResult` rows at `data.items[]`, each `{ title, url, description }` (inferred from a sample): {title string, url string, description string}.

Page-level: `data.dropped`, `data.empty_reason`, `data.empty_reason_note`, `data.walk`.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/google/search" \
  --data-urlencode "query=best restaurants in London" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## Withdrawn endpoints (do not call)

These stay registered but return `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` today and never bill. A permanent withdrawal is not coming back - use the alternative named in the platform's other endpoints rather than retrying.

- `GET /v1/google/ai-mode` - temporarily withdrawn while its data source is re-established. Returns `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` and never bills; check the changelog before retrying.
- `GET /v1/google/flights` - temporarily withdrawn while its data source is re-established. Returns `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` and never bills; check the changelog before retrying.
